A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a real [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] and $p$ a [[Definition:Sublinear Functional|sublinear functional]] on $X$.
Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Linear Functional|linear functional]] on a [[Definition:Vector Subspace|subspace]] $M$ with $f \le p$ on $M$.
Then there is a linear functional $F$ on $X$ extending $f$ with $F \le p$ on $X$.

B_source.statement: Every [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] has a [[Definition:Basis (Linear Algebra)|basis]]: the [[Definition:Linearly Independent Set|linearly independent]] sets, ordered by inclusion, satisfy the hypotheses of [[Zorn's Lemma]], and a maximal one cannot be extended by any further vector.

substitutions.adding one vector: extending g to N + R x_0

derived.a maximal independent set: a dominated extension defined on all of X

object_map.reformulation: Reuse the Zorn's Lemma pattern of the basis theorem: show chains have upper bounds and that a non-total element can be extended by one more dimension.

validity_conditions: The one-dimensional extension step must preserve the bound by p, which is the real content of the argument.
The axiom of choice, through Zorn's Lemma, is required in general.
proof_plan: Let $\EE$ be the set of pairs $\tuple {N, g}$ with $M \subseteq N$ a subspace, $g$ linear on $N$ extending $f$, and $g \le p$ on $N$, ordered by extension.

The union of a chain in $\EE$ is again in $\EE$, so every chain has an upper bound.
By [[Zorn's Lemma]], $\EE$ has a maximal element $\tuple {N, g}$.

Suppose $N \ne X$ and pick $x_0 \notin N$.
For $n, n' \in N$, $\map g n + \map g {n'} \le \map p {n - x_0} + \map p {n' + x_0}$, so:
:$\displaystyle \sup_{n \mathop \in N} \paren {\map g n - \map p {n - x_0} } \le \inf_{n' \mathop \in N} \paren {\map p {n' + x_0} - \map g {n'} }$
Setting $\map g {x_0} = c$ for any $c$ between these bounds extends $g$ to $N + \R x_0$ with $g \le p$, contradicting maximality.
